issues.description: Return type of Stock.take is inconsistent: the problem statement (UML) and the solution implementation declare Stock.take(String) to return an int (returning the remaining quantity or -1 on failure), whereas the template's Stock.take(String) returns a boolean. This mismatch will confuse students implementing SealSaloon methods (which rely on take returning an int) and can cause compilation or logic errors when following the specification or the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template's Stock.take method signature and implementation to match the UML and solution: change the return type from boolean to int and return the remaining quantity on success or -1 on failure (when ingredient not found or quantity < 1). Alternatively, if boolean semantics are intended, update the problem statement and solution to use boolean consistently. Prefer aligning the template to the UML/solution so students can follow the specification and examples.
